newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian troops kill eight rebels, capture 20.
newsitem.headline: Colombian troops kill eight rebels, capture 20.

text.p: Government troops killed eight leftist guerrillas and captured 20 others in the latest round of fighting across Colombia, military spokesmen said on Tuesday.

Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra said, meanwhile, that the government was planning on calling up military reserves to counter the growing threat posed by rebels, who have unleashed a wave of attacks since late last month in which at least 200 people have been killed.

A statement from the military high command said eight Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels died in fighting on Monday and on Tuesday in northwest Antioquia province and central Cundinamarca, the province that rings the capital.
Some 25 FARC guerrillas were killed in combat and military air strikes over the weekend in Antioquia.

The statement said 20 members of the FARC had also been captured by army troops in southwestern Putumayo, the jungle-covered province where at least 60 soliders were taken prisoner by the FARC on Aug. 30.
It was not immediately clear if the captured rebels would be used as a bargaining chip to win the release of the soldiers.

In an interview published in Tuesday's editions of El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, Esguerra said an undetermined number of Colombia's 120-strong military reserves would be called up in early October to boost the military's fighting capacity.

He offered no details, but Army chief Gen. Harold Bedoya has complained in recent interviews that the military was too small to mount an effective counterinsurgency campaign. "We have 100,000 soldiers for a country that should have at least 360,000," Bedoya said.

The National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second-largest guerrilla army after the FARC, has dynamited the country's main oil pipeline, erected roadblocks across major highways and torched at least 50 vehicles since it launched a nationwide offensive against the government of President Ernesto Samper on Friday.
The attacks included one at dawn on Tuesday in which ELN guerrillas set 10 buses and three private vehicles on fire in a parking lot on the outskirts of Cali, Colombia's second largest city.
